name: AgentsView Task Control Plane
goal: Build a thin local-first, event-driven agent task control plane with a Kanban board, harness-neutral agent management, compact context, session intelligence, task types, phases, gates, and metrics.
repoContext: Clean AgentsView main checkout: Go daemon/CLI, SQLite archive, REST/SSE server, provider parsers, and Svelte 5 frontend. Task state will use a separate local tasks.db.

stories.title: Add the Kanban and agent UI
Connect tasks, sessions, intelligence, and runtime
Activate managed runtime from the daemon
Expose task detail and aggregate metrics
Add ticket detail, live session, and metrics dashboard routes
Attach deliverables to task details (screenshots, git diffs, bounded files/links)

eventLog.event: User directed remaining questions be inferred and implementation begin with subagents.
PRD, architecture, and story gates auto-approved.
Integrated storage/API, Kanban UI, harness runtime, CLI/MCP, and dispatch slices.
User established lifecycle authority: implementing agents own Understand through Verify; coordinator owns only gated Verify to Done.
Created and assigned three full-lifecycle dogfood tickets for runtime activation, metrics API, and ticket detail/dashboard views.
User expanded ticket detail to require the actual active or linked agent session and bounded live activity.

QA pass: focused + full Go suites (10848 tests), vet, frontend check/kit-ui/tests/build all green; remotesync flake did not recur. Moved task-runtime-activation, task-metrics-api, task-ticket-views to Done/Deliver with gate evidence.

Root-caused why ticket detail shows no agent session for any task, including In Progress ones: RunCoordinator.persistSessionLink only fires from a live taskrun.Event emitted by the managed runtime, which has never been activated (daemon task_runtime.enabled stays off by default, no worktree ever created). Not a frontend bug; session_links/agent_session are correctly empty because no real run has ever dispatched.

Added a pulsing border animation to Kanban TaskCard when an active session link exists, respecting prefers-reduced-motion; verified live in browser via temporary DOM class toggle, no real session data touched.

Created S10 for the new task-deliverable-attachments ticket. Decisive next step remains unstarted: enable [task_runtime] in the daemon config and let it spawn a real agent process against one ticket to prove the full lifecycle + session-link + deliverable-attachment loop.

User asked whether Verify actually works. Confirmed it does not: defaultTaskGateEvaluator (huma_routes_tasks.go:694) trusts caller-asserted evidence.passed/approved and never reads gate.Rule/Config; WithTaskGateEvaluator (server.go:320) is never wired into the real daemon. Every gate, including the three closed in Iteration 3, passed on self-attestation. Corrected the FEEDBACK_REPORT.md Iteration 3 record. Filed S11/task_41ed1720fc3a1e59d11bc2c3 with an explicit unresolved design question (execute gate.Rule server-side vs. check a verifiable artifact reference) for the user to answer before implementation. Surfaced gate rule/evidence/evaluated_at and a per-ticket Verify-to-Execute rework count in ticket detail so the self-attestation gap is visible instead of hidden.

User chose option 1 for S11: execute gate.Rule server-side. Implemented ruleGateEvaluator (internal/server/task_gate_evaluator.go), wired via taskGateEvaluatorOption whenever task_runtime.repository is configured (independent of task_runtime.enabled, which stays off). Set [task_runtime] repository in ~/.agentsview/config.toml (machine-local, not tracked) and restarted the dev daemon to pick it up. Verified live end-to-end on the persistent daemon: a failing rule stayed failed and a passing rule stayed passed even when the caller asserted the opposite via approved/evidence.passed. Filed evidence on task_41ed1720fc3a1e59d11bc2c3 and moved it to Done. Gates evaluated in Iteration 3 (task-runtime-activation, task-metrics-api, task-ticket-views) were not retroactively re-verified and remain on their original self-attested evidence.

notes: Single-user and local-machine v1; no hosting.
